design: RMIT (randomized multiple interleaved trials): fresh random permutation of (strategy, concurrency) pairs per repetition; server restarted before every run.
caveats: An active Claude Code agent session was running on this same laptop during this run (consuming some CPU/RAM), so the manual 'close every other application' step in docs/rmit_experiment_protocol.md was not satisfied. Load average during runs was frequently 4-12 on a 4-thread CPU, well above idle, from both benchmark client threads and this background session. Despite that, throughput was highly stable (see rmit_analysis_summary.csv: relative 95% CI width <=0.039 for all 48 configurations, no bimodal states detected). This run is suitable as the first RMIT dataset and as validation that the design works, but a from-idle rerun is worth doing for the final paper numbers.
